panels.title: How to use this page
panels.description: Read me first.

options.content:
**Green = working. Red = look now.** Times follow the picker at the top right. Nothing to type: click.

| You are | Start here |
|---|---|
| **Operations** | The tiles under *Is everything working?* Any red tile or line in *What is wrong right now* says what to do (click it). |
| **Support** | A user quotes a **request id** (from an error message) or a **run id**: paste it in *Find a run, request or job id* at the top, then open *Follow one run or request*. Or click any blue id on this page. |
| **Developers** | *Errors and exceptions* lists every bug with its traceback (click a row, then the request or run id for the whole story). *What is slow* shows where time goes. |

panels.title: Is everything working?
panels.description: Operations: one look tells whether every part is up.

panels.title: Overall
panels.description: ALL GOOD when no alert is on; else how many problems, listed just below (also those just noticed and still being checked).

panels.title: Parts of the system
panels.description: WORKING = fine. DOWN = broken: the matching line in 'What is wrong right now' says what to do. UNKNOWN = the API is down, so it cannot check. Workers: a live worker takes that queue's jobs (find threats; write scenarios; map controls; write remediation plans; map services; maintenance = reaper, library search, threat intelligence). Scheduler = Celery beat, which starts the reaper every minute: WORKING when the reaper finished a pass in the last 5 minutes (a worker that has just started counts as on time). AI service, from real calls in the last 10 minutes: WORKING, SOME ERRORS, NOT ANSWERING (over half failed), or IDLE (no calls). Log collection = Loki and Alloy; Alerting = Alertmanager.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(tsg_ai_calls_total[10m])) == 0) * 0 + 3 or (sum(increase(tsg_ai_calls_total{outcome!~"ok|truncated"}[10m])) / sum(increase(tsg_ai_calls_total[10m])) > 0.5) * 0 + 4 or (sum(increase(tsg_ai_calls_total{outcome!~"ok|truncated"}[10m])) > 0) * 0 + 2 or (sum(increase(tsg_ai_calls_total[10m])) > 0) * 0 + 1 or vector(-1)

panels.title: What the workers are doing
panels.description: Operations and developers: the Celery workers' jobs, now and over time.

panels.title: Jobs running now
panels.description: Jobs each worker is running at this moment (from Flower). 0 everywhere and jobs waiting = stuck.

panels.title: Jobs waiting in each queue
panels.description: Jobs sent but not yet picked up by a worker, a run's next stages and new work together. Growing for long = the workers cannot keep up (or are down).

panels.title: Jobs finished, by result
panels.description: Jobs ended per 5 minutes (the every-minute reaper and the 15 s looks of a job waiting for another job left out): done, tried again after an outage, failed.

panels.title: Report card per job type
panels.description: For each kind of job in the chosen time: how many were done, tried again and failed, and how long 95 % of them took.

panels.title: Jobs now, by kind and status
panels.description: How many jobs of each kind are waiting, waiting to try again, or running right now, and how many failed in the last 24 hours. The reaper counts them once a minute. For the jobs themselves, with their errors and workers: GET /v1/admin/jobs.

defaults.noValue: No job waiting, running or failed

panels.title: What is slow
panels.description: Developers: where the time goes. 95 % of calls finish within the time shown.

panels.title: Slowest job types
panels.description: How long 95 % of each kind of job took in the chosen time, slowest first.

panels.title: Slowest AI steps
panels.description: How long 95 % of the AI calls of each step took, slowest first. Above a minute: the AI gateway is slow (see docs/UAT_LLM_TIMEOUT_RUNBOOK.md).

panels.title: Slowest API pages
panels.description: How long 95 % of the calls to each API address took (probes left out), slowest first.

panels.title: AI capacity in use
panels.description: AI calls running now, out of the limit in force: CII_MAX_CONCURRENT_AI_CALLS or the one a gateway 429 set, the lower (0 = none). A 429 sets that limit to half the calls in flight at that moment; each answer raises it a little, and it is gone a few minutes after the last 429. At 100 % new calls wait for a free slot. No limit set: TSG runs at full speed.

panels.title: AI call time over time (95 %)
panels.description: How long 95 % of AI calls took, per step. A climb = the AI gateway slows down.

panels.title: Job time over time (95 %)
panels.description: How long 95 % of jobs took, per job type.

panels.title: Wait for a worker over time (95 %)
panels.description: How long 95 % of jobs waited after they were due until a worker took them, per job type. A climb = too few worker threads for the work sent.

panels.title: Traffic: API and AI calls
panels.description: Operations: how busy the system is, and how much of it fails.

panels.title: API calls per minute
panels.description: Calls to the API by result (health probes left out).

panels.title: Share of API calls that are server errors
panels.description: Health probes left out (/ready answers 503 on purpose). The alert Api5xxHigh fires above 2 %.

panels.title: AI calls per minute
panels.description: AI calls by result: answered, no answer (outage), unusable answer, error.

panels.title: Wait for an AI request's turn (95 %), by model
panels.description: How long 95 % of each model's AI requests waited for their turn under that model's own requests-a-minute limit (CII_CHAT_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE, CII_CHAT_FALLBACK_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE, CII_EMBEDDING_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE, CII_RERANK_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE); a request that did not wait counts as 0, and a model with no limit (0) has no line. Above 30 s for 10 minutes fires AiRequestRateWaitHigh for that model: more work is sent to it than its limit allows, so jobs slow down.

panels.title: AI gateway refusals (429) per minute
panels.description: HTTP 429 answers from the AI gateway per minute, by model: that model's own requests-a-minute limit was hit and the call waits and tries again. Stays at 0 while each model's setting (CII_CHAT_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE and its siblings) is below that model's limit.
